svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: histostate: how the tissue classifier is trained and checked
svg.desc: Training runs on a laptop or, for sweeps, as AWS Batch jobs launched by Nextflow. PathMNIST comes from Zenodo; the test set from a second clinical center is split into shift-val for tuning and a final test scored once.
svg.text: Dashed boxes are outside AWS. Open the SVG on its own and hover a box for what it does and why.

g.title: Every stage runs here. AWS is only for sweeps.
Built with Terraform in us-east-1. Billed only while jobs run.
Where the tiles come from and which split answers which question.
What runs before code reaches main.

a.title: Trains the CNN locally. Picks an NVIDIA GPU, then the Apple GPU (MPS), then CPU. A 64-pixel run is 60 epochs at about 12 s each on an M-series Mac.
The command-line tool: resizes an image to the model's tile size, applies the saved training mean and spread, and prints the top three tissue types with probabilities.
Saves the learned filters, the activation maps for example tiles, and the tiles that most excite the strongest stroma/muscle feature. This is how the stain shortcut was found.
Scores a saved model on validation and on the final test half. Run once per chosen model; tuning against it would turn it into another validation set.
Turns a sweep such as --jitters 0.3,0.5 --seeds 1,2 into one AWS Batch job per pair, stages files through S3, retries jobs whose Spot instance is reclaimed, and records time and memory per job.
a.text: one job per jitter and seed

a.title: Packages the code and the locked dependencies from uv.lock into one image. The PyTorch wheels carry the CUDA libraries, so a plain python:3.14-slim base is enough.
Terraform describes every AWS resource in three stacks (bootstrap, foundation, training), checked by terraform test against a mocked provider, and applies a plan only after it is reviewed.
Trained weights plus the training mean and spread, the tile size, and the block count, so ask and evaluate_test rebuild the same model. Not committed to git.
Three job queues. Batch starts an EC2 instance for each job and scales back to zero when the queue is empty, so idle time costs nothing.

GPU jobs run on g4dn.xlarge (NVIDIA T4) or g5.xlarge (A10G); CPU jobs on 8 vCPU c6i, c7i, or m6i instances. Each job pulls the image and downloads PathMNIST from Zenodo. Spot reclaimed both GPU instances mid-run once, so the 64-pixel runs used on-demand.
a.text: g4dn / g5 GPU, c6i / c7i / m6i

a.title: Private registry for the training image. Batch instances pull it with their own IAM role, so no registry login lives on the instance.

What Terraform created, kept in a versioned, private S3 bucket so the next plan knows what exists. A $100 monthly budget alerts on everything tagged project=histostate. Batch uses the account's default VPC.
Nextflow's working files under work/, deleted after 30 days, and the checkpoints and logs under results/. Encrypted, public access blocked.
MedMNIST's copy of the colorectal tiles as NumPy files, pre-split. CC BY 4.0.
Training and validation tiles. Validation is a random slice of the same pool, so it can't see the staining shift.
The official test set, from a different clinical center with different staining. split_test cuts it into two stratified halves.
SGD with gradient clipping and cosine decay; flips, rotations, and color jitter on training batches; keeps the epoch with the best validation accuracy.
Half of the second center's tiles. Every setting is compared here, three seeds each.
A gap counts only when the seed ranges don't overlap. Under shift, seeds disagree several times more than on validation.
The other half. Scored once per chosen model, after every decision is made.
64 pixels, 3 conv blocks, 93,193 weights, color jitter 0.3. 94.0% on shift-val and 94.7% on final test; stroma and smooth muscle are still its weakest pair.
Lint and format run before a commit lands.
main is protected: every change arrives as a pull request and is squash-merged.
CI on every pull request. --locked fails if pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree.
Hand-written softmax, gradients, and convolutions checked against PyTorch, plus augmentation, splits, the model shapes, and the ask command.
